summary: Triaged the two mounted targets on the Debian stable toolchain (clang 19.1.7, go 1.24.4): a libFuzzer run on c-record hit the off-by-one stack-buffer-overflow in lab_parse_records (record.c:28) after 20334 execs, minimized to a 20-byte reproducer and replayed through the ASan+UBSan build; `go test -fuzz` caught the index-out-of-range panic in ParseField (field.go:24) and minimised the input to the corpus file "0:". Two unique crashes, one per track.

findings.title: Off-by-one stack-buffer-overflow in lab_parse_records
findings.description: The timed libFuzzer campaign reached a type-1 record with a 16-byte name: rlen > sizeof(name) is 16 > 16, false, memcpy fills name[0..15] and the terminator write name[16] lands one byte past the buffer. ASan reports WRITE of size 1 at record.c:28 overflowing 'name'; UBSan flags the same line first. Minimised reproducer is 20 bytes.
findings.remediation: Change the bounds check to rlen >= sizeof(name) so a 16-byte name is rejected before memcpy, keeping the terminator inside the buffer.

findings.title: ParseField panics on a line ending with the separator
findings.description: ParseField("0:") finds the ':' at index 1, leaves rest empty, then reads rest[0] and panics with index out of range. `go test -fuzz` found a 38-byte failing input and minimised it to the corpus entry "0:".
findings.remediation: Check len(rest) before indexing: treat a line ending in ':' as a field with an empty value or as ErrNoSeparator, and add 'Name:' to the seed corpus.
